job.title: Backend Engineer
job.description: Build and operate Python APIs backed by PostgreSQL and Redis, deployed with Docker on Kubernetes.

knowledge_items.content: Ask how they decide which columns to index in PostgreSQL, when a composite index beats single-column indexes, and how they verify a query uses it with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
Ask how they manage database connections under load: connection pooling, pgbouncer, pool sizing, and what happens when the pool is exhausted.
Ask how they keep a Redis cache consistent with the database: write-through versus cache-aside, TTLs, and invalidating keys when data changes.
A strong answer on Redis memory management mentions maxmemory, eviction policies such as allkeys-lru, key expiry, and monitoring hit rate.
Ask how they keep Docker images small and builds fast: multi-stage builds, layer caching, slim base images, and running as a non-root user.
Ask how they roll out a new version on Kubernetes without downtime: rolling updates, readiness probes, resource limits, and rollback.
Ask when to use async def versus def in FastAPI, what blocks the event loop, and how they run CPU-heavy or blocking work.
A strong answer on background jobs covers idempotent tasks, retries with exponential backoff, dead-letter handling, and visibility timeouts.
Ask them to design a rate limiter for a public API: token bucket versus sliding window, where state lives, and behaviour across multiple servers.
Ask how they secure an API with JWTs: token expiry, refresh tokens, key rotation, and where tokens must never be stored.
A strong answer on testing separates fast unit tests from integration tests against a real database, uses fixtures, and tests failure paths, not only the happy path.
Ask how they debug a production incident: structured logs, request IDs, metrics, tracing, and how they find the root cause quickly.

knowledge_queries.q: We added a multi-column index on user id and created at, and checked the query plan to make sure it was used.
Our app kept running out of database connections during traffic spikes, so we put a pooler in front.
When a record changes we delete the cached key and let the next read repopulate it with a short expiry.
The cache was growing without limit so we set a memory cap and a least-recently-used eviction policy.
I use a multi-stage build and a slim base image so the final container is tiny.
We do rolling deployments with readiness probes so pods only get traffic when healthy, and we can roll back fast.
A synchronous library call was freezing all requests, so I moved it to a thread pool instead of an async handler.
Our background tasks retry with backoff and are safe to run twice, and failures land in a dead letter queue.
I would use a token bucket stored in a shared store so every server enforces the same request limit per client.
Access tokens expire in fifteen minutes, refresh tokens rotate, and we never keep tokens in local storage.
We keep quick isolated unit tests and also run integration tests against a real database including the error paths.
Every request has an id in the logs and we use traces and metrics to find which service slowed down.

resume_text:
Priya Nair
Senior Backend Engineer

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 6 years of experience building high-traffic APIs in Python. Comfortable owning services from design to on-call.

EXPERIENCE
PaySphere (2021 to present): Led the migration of a monolith to FastAPI microservices handling 3,000 requests per second. Reduced p95 latency from 800ms to 120ms by adding Redis caching and composite PostgreSQL indexes.

LogiTrack (2018 to 2021): Built the real-time shipment tracking backend. Introduced Celery workers with retry and backoff for carrier webhooks, processing two million events a day.

INFRASTRUCTURE
Packaged services with Docker multi-stage builds and deployed to Kubernetes with rolling updates and readiness probes. Built CI pipelines in GitHub Actions.

EDUCATION
B.Tech in Computer Science, NIT Calicut, 2018.

CERTIFICATIONS
AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate. Completed a course on distributed systems and consensus.

VOLUNTEERING
Mentors students at a local coding club every weekend and organises hackathons.
